On listening to structure

There is a particular pleasure in reading a well-formed document. The sections follow one another the way phrases follow one another in a song, and the headings act like cadences that let you breathe before the next idea arrives.

When markup is honest, the outline is the melody. Nothing needs to be decorated to be understood, and nothing needs to shout to be heard.

Small pages, long thoughts

A modest page with three articles and a handful of links has a completely different texture from a dashboard bristling with buttons. That difference should be audible, not merely visible, and this fixture exists to prove that it is.

Margins

Wide margins are rests. White space is silence. A blog is mostly silence with a little structure floating in it, which is why it should sound like slow piano over a warm pad rather than a drum machine.
